conventions.convention: The DCT-I is unnormalised: X_k=y_0+(-1)^k y_n+2 sum_{j=1}^{n-1} y_j cos(jkπ/n), for n≥1. Samples run from the right endpoint to the left endpoint; interior sums are empty at n=1.
Chebyshev reconstruction uses a_0=X_0/(2n), a_n=X_n/(2n), and a_k=X_k/n for 1≤k<n.
For a<b, m=(a+b)/2 and d=(b-a)/2, quadrature is d times the integrated normalized interpolant. At n=0 it is explicitly (b-a)f(m), without calling the DCT-I.

The residual is integral minus quadrature. The Peano truncated power is zero when x≤t; at order one it is the indicator of x>t. Nodes may repeat, weights may be signed, and exactness explicitly includes the zero polynomial.
Bernoulli polynomials have B_0=1 and the displayed normalized antiderivative recursion; B_m denotes B_m(0), so B_1(x)=x−1/2.
Romberg levels start at ℓ=0 with 2^ℓ panels; columns satisfy 0≤j≤ℓ≤L and use denominator 4^j−1.
The eight-panel Newton–Cotes rule is on [-1,1], with nodes −1+j/4 and weights (989,5888,−928,10496,−4540,10496,−928,5888,989)/14175.

The computed Clenshaw–Curtis procedure requires representable samples for n≥1, propagates the DFT supplier's failure statuses, and performs postprocessing in exact real arithmetic. It asserts no end-to-end floating-point accuracy or stability bound.

load_bearing.statement: For n≥1 and g∈C[-1,1], the stated DCT-I coefficients give p_n(t)=sum_{k=0}^n a_k T_k(t), the unique polynomial of degree at most n interpolating g at cos(jπ/n); in particular p_n=I_n^L g.

For a<b, integers N,p≥1, h=(b-a)/N and f∈C^{2p}([a,b]), T_N equals the integral plus the endpoint Bernoulli corrections through r=p minus h^{2p}/(2p)! times the sum of panel integrals of B_{2p}((x-x_i)/h)f^{(2p)}(x). The remainder has absolute value at most (b-a)M_{2p}h^{2p}||f^{(2p)}||∞/(2p)!.

For a<b, a finite real weighted quadrature, integer r≥1, exactness on the zero polynomial and all nonzero polynomials of degree at most r−1, and f∈C^r([a,b]), L(f)=∫_a^b K_r(t)f^{(r)}(t)dt and |L(f)|≤(∫_a^b |K_r(t)|dt)||f^{(r)}||∞.

For the nodes x_j=−1+j/4 and rule Q_8, the weights are the integrals of the degree-eight Lagrange cardinal polynomials. Interpreting polynomial inputs by their evaluation functions, the rule is exact for the zero polynomial and every nonzero formal polynomial of degree at most 9.
For n≥1 and 0≤k,ℓ≤n, the half-endpoint weighted cosine product sum is n at matching endpoint frequencies, n/2 at matching interior frequencies, and zero for k≠ℓ.
For k≥0, μ_k=∫_{−1}^1 T_k(x)dx equals 2 for k=0, zero for odd k, and 2/(1−k²) for even k≥2.
For a<b, j≥1 and f∈C^{2j+2}([a,b]), every N≥1 satisfies T_N(f)=I+sum_{r=1}^j c_r h^{2r}+ε_N with |ε_N|≤C_j h^{2j+2}, where the displayed finite C_j is independent of N.
For m≥1, B'_m=mB_{m−1} and ∫_0^1 B_m=0. Endpoint values agree for m≥2; B_m(1−x)=(−1)^mB_m(x) for m≥0; odd Bernoulli numbers vanish for m≥3; each B_m is bounded on [0,1].

For a<b, n∈N and f∈C[a,b], Q_{n,[a,b]} is exact on zero and every nonzero formal polynomial of degree at most n, and |∫_a^b f−Q_{n,[a,b]}(f)|≤(b-a)(1+Λ_n^L)E_n(g), where g(t)=f(m+dt). Affine pullback identifies E_n(g) with the best degree-n uniform error on [a,b].
